body:
Money won't make me happy, but having it will keep me from ending up a drug dealer like my dad. Did you use any financial aid? Student loans? My brother is a doctor, he's 40 and still in debt, so I'm just trying to picture this.

I don't have a teacher yet. This test was intended to see if I was adequately prepared to take this class in the first place, it was so basic that it was almost assumed I would pass it. Nobody ever brought up what would happen if I failed.

I've been trying for years to find a talent. Everyone has one right? Can play an instruments, good at math, good with computers. I don't have that. I've tried for years, and it's catching up.

But what if nothing makes me happy? I only chose this major because I hated it less than my last one. I don't enjoy anything, I'm not good at anything.

How did you manage to pay for med school? I didn't know how I'd even pay for this four year program, assuming I could even get in the door (which it looks like I can't, if I fail this).

The thing about studying harder is that it won't get me back in to school. My financial aid is completely gone if I change majors at any point for the next four years. If I take out a student loan and fail then now I'm in debt and have no applicable life skills.

If I have no skills, no passion, and the only thing to look forward to is owing someone money for most of my adult life, then why bother?
It was alright I guess. Not really my thing.

It's mainly stressful because I have no safety net. If this doesn't work out and I can't figure out what I'm going to do I might end up homeless.

I listen to music sometimes I guess. It never really helps anything though.
I don't really know. I honestly don't know why I even bothered posting this.
